chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, a group from the Banu Umayya, during the emirate of Uthman, gathered in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on a Friday. They wanted to marry a man from among them, and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was nearby. Some of them said to others, 'Shall we shame Ali at this moment? We will ask him to address us, and we will keep talking, for he will be shy and weary of speech.' So they approached him and said, 'O Abu al-Hasan! We want to marry so-and-so to so-and-so, and we want you to address us.' He said, 'Are you waiting for anyone?' They said, 'No.'

By Allah, he did not delay long before he said: 'Praise is to Allah, the One particularized with Oneness, the Foremost with Warning, the Doer of what He wills, the Veiled by Light from His creation, the Possessor of the Lofty Horizon and the Exalted Honor and the Luxurious Kingdom, worshipped for His Bounties, Lord of the Earth and the Sky. I praise Him for the beauty of affliction and the grace of giving and the plenteous blessings, and for what our Lord defends from affliction; a praise for which the servants begin and upon which the lands flourish. And I testify that there is no god but Allah, One, with no partner, for whom there was no thing before, and for whom there will be no thing after.'

And I testify that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is His servant and His Messenger, whom He chose with preference and guided by him from misguidance. He singled him out for Himself and sent him to His creation with His messages and His speech, inviting them to His worship, His Oneness, and acknowledgment of His Lordship, and belief in His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). He sent him at a time of interval from the Messengers, when people had turned away from the Truth, were ignorant of the Lord, and disbelieved in the Resurrection and the Warning. So he delivered His messages, strove in His way, advised his community, and worshipped Him until death came to him. May Allah bless him and his family abundantly.

I advise you and myself with the fear of Allah the Magnificent. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made for the pious an exit from what they dislike and sustenance from where they do not expect. So fulfill Allah's promise and seek what is with Him through obedience to Him and acting upon what He loves. For goodness is not attained except through it, nor is what is with Him attained except through obedience to Him. And do not rely on anything else for what is to come, except upon Him. And there is no might and no strength except with Allah.

Thereafter, indeed Allah has finalized matters and established them according to their measures, so they do not deviate from their courses until they reach their ends, in what He has decreed and judged. And among what He has decreed and judged from His definite command and finalized judgments is that which has caused the generations to branch out and causes to flow, and He judged the conclusion of judgments for us and for you to be present in this gathering, which Allah has singled us and you out for, to remember His bounties, the beauty of His trials, and the manifestation of His blessings.

So we ask Allah for us and for you the blessing of what gathered us and you to it and brought us and you to it. Then, so-and-so son of so-and-so has proposed so-and-so daughter of so-and-so, and he is of the lineage you know and of the nobility you do not ignore, and he has given her the dowry you know. So return good, that you may be praised for it and attributed to it. May Allah bless Muhammad and his family and grant them peace.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (as) respond to the Banu Umayya's challenge to shame him during a marriage sermon?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi*, this hadith highlights the political and rhetorical contest between Imam Ali (AS) and the Banu Umayya during the Umayyad governorship, where they attempted to mock his perceived shyness (*hilm*) by challenging him to deliver the marriage sermon (*khutbah*). Instead of faltering, Imam Ali delivered a masterful oration that combined theological depth, praise of Allah, and the legal conclusion of the marriage, thereby transforming their trap into a demonstration of his supreme eloquence and authority. This event is often cited in Shia scholarship to illustrate the concept of *I'jaz* (inimitability) in the Imams' speech and their ability to command respect even from political adversaries.
